items.grounds: Re-derived both ways from bytes. כִּ֣י opens oshb:Isa.8.23 (= web:Isa.9.1) verse-initially (byte tier), and the particle's skeleton also opens oshb:Isa.9.3 (= web:Isa.9.4), oshb:Isa.9.4 (= web:Isa.9.5) and oshb:Isa.9.5 (= web:Isa.9.6) as each verse's first token (token-bound skeleton tier, 3/3) — the row's own showing disqualifies the only formal marker it names. What remains as shipped is thematic ('the seam rests on the turn from darkened lands to light and glory the verse carries, not on the particle' — verified verbatim); no ruled tier-1 class (frame onset, speech formula, vocative, imperative onset, addressee shift) is named at the seam verse, and the row's oss key oracle_frame.light_dawning_onset names no ruled frame class of the book's tier-1 spine (massa/hoy/koh-amar/neum/vocative/imperative/addressee-shift), so it supplies no formal onset either; pmarks_Isa.json re-checked: no parashah entry at MT 8:22 (tier-3 layer, single-witness, absence never counterevidence). The unused byte-anchored candidate is real: כָּעֵ֣ת הָרִאשׁ֗וֹן and וְהָאַחֲר֖וֹן הִכְבִּ֑יד both collate at byte tier inside oshb:Isa.8.23 (= web:Isa.9.1), in that order (byte offsets 43 and 112), and neither run appears anywhere in the shipped rationale. The seam's placement itself is uncontested (the preceding row closes at web:Isa.8.22; no span change filed), and the span carries the registered expected-low-confidence stack at oshb:Isa.9.5-9.6 (= web:Isa.9.6-9.7): defective front-seam warrant, not alone load-bearing — confirm at medium.

Both warring sentences verified verbatim in the shipped rationale: the concession 'not because no fresh subject or addressee arises — both do', which itself names הָעָם֙ הַהֹלְכִ֣ים בַּחֹ֔שֶׁךְ (oshb:Isa.9.1 = web:Isa.9.2, byte tier, re-collated) as the fresh nominal subject and הִרְבִּ֣יתָ הַגּ֔וֹי (oshb:Isa.9.2 = web:Isa.9.3, byte tier, re-collated) as the second-person turn, against the closing 'No addressee or subject marker reopens before web:Isa.9.8's fresh declarative sentence' (web:Isa.9.8 = oshb:Isa.9.7). Unscoped, the closing universal is falsified by the field's own two named markers; only an explicit rescope after the birth clause at oshb:Isa.9.5 (= web:Isa.9.6) would save it, and the field does not say that — the audit's reading is byte-true. The rear seam survives independently, as the finding files: דָּבָ֛ר שָׁלַ֥ח אֲדֹנָ֖י (oshb:Isa.9.7, byte tier) = web:Isa.9.8 opens the following unit's fresh declarative subject, and pmarks_Isa.json carries SAMEKH at MT 9:6 (= WEB 9:7; tier-3, single-witness). Self-contradictory closing warrant, boundary unaffected: confirm at medium.

Byte-verified in full. The doubled pair לםרבה לְמַרְבֵּ֨ה collates at byte tier and opens oshb:Isa.9.6 (= web:Isa.9.7) at byte offset 0; WEB's rendering of that clause opens the verse — “Of the increase of his government” (web:Isa.9.7 = oshb:Isa.9.6), normalized position 0 — while the row's paired gloss “The zeal of Yahweh of Armies will perform this.” (web:Isa.9.7 = oshb:Isa.9.6) is the verse-final sentence (normalized position 212 of 259) rendering קִנְאַ֛ת יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת תַּעֲשֶׂה זֹּֽאת (oshb:Isa.9.6 = web:Isa.9.7, byte tier, verse-final): splice and gloss render disjoint clauses, so the shipped 'rendered' is false under any parse — the core defect, exactly as filed. Both extent mismatches also re-derive: the six-token splice כִּ֣י לֹ֣א מוּעָף֮ לַאֲשֶׁ֣ר מוּצָ֣ק לָהּ֒ (oshb:Isa.8.23 = web:Isa.9.1, byte tier) is paired with the row's whole-verse gloss of web:Isa.9.1 (= oshb:Isa.8.23) — normalized equality with the full verse verified — whose opening sentence alone renders the splice; and the throne-name gloss's opening words render וַיִּקְרָ֨א שְׁמ֜וֹ (oshb:Isa.9.5 = web:Isa.9.6, byte tier), which sits immediately before the splice and outside it (byte offset 83; splice at 103, adjacent). Those two keep splice overlap in the corpus's tolerated onset-splice-with-fuller-gloss shape; the closing pair overlaps nothing. Not load-bearing: the close at web:Isa.9.7 (= oshb:Isa.9.6) stands on the SAMEKH after MT 9:6 (= WEB 9:7; tier-3, single-witness) plus the fresh subject at web:Isa.9.8 (= oshb:Isa.9.7). Confirm at medium.

Adversarially re-derived over the full range in both witnesses. All 14 verses oshb:Isa.9.7-Isa.9.20 (= web:Isa.9.8-Isa.9.21) were scanned for second-person markers (word-final kaf; 2mp/2fp qatal endings; word-final tav+qamats; independent second-person pronouns): 1 formal hit, יְסַכְסֵֽךְ (oshb:Isa.9.10 = web:Isa.9.11, byte tier), byte-reviewed as that verse's final word, a third-person verb whose final kaf is the root's own final radical — WEB renders “and will stir up his enemies,” (web:Isa.9.11 = oshb:Isa.9.10) — plus a you/your sweep over web:Isa.9.8-Isa.9.21 (= oshb:Isa.9.7-Isa.9.20): 0 matches in 14 verses. Zero second-person forms stand in the stanzas, so the shipped 'the nation addressed in the preceding stanzas' is byte-false in exactly the register the corpus made load-bearing: the poem's opening-stanza row (span Isa.9.8-Isa.9.12, WEB; = oshb:Isa.9.7-Isa.9.11) rests its own seam on 'no second-person verb or suffix appears' across oshb:Isa.9.7-Isa.9.11 (= web:Isa.9.8-Isa.9.12) — re-verified true inside my scan — and on the shift being 'of the oracle's target rather than of addressee'. One narration slip in the finding: that row is not the one 'shipped immediately before this one' — the immediately preceding row spans Isa.9.18-Isa.9.21 (WEB; = oshb:Isa.9.17-Isa.9.20), and its own rejected_alternative says 'the addressee shifts from the punished nation', sharing the loose usage — but the filed incompatibility between shipped neighbours is real either way. The front seam stands untouched on the woe-onset ה֥וֹי הַחֹֽקְקִ֖ים (oshb:Isa.10.1, byte tier). Byte-false supporting claim, not alone load-bearing: confirm at medium.

Byte-derived: כִּ֖י יֹאמַ֑ר collates at byte tier as the verse-initial two-token opening of oshb:Isa.10.8, and WEB renders that formula as the verse-opening “For he says,” (web:Isa.10.8) — normalized position 0, length 12 — while the row's paired gloss “Aren’t all of my princes kings?” (web:Isa.10.8) begins at normalized position 14: fully disjoint extents, zero overlap, so the pairing presents the boast clause as the rendering of the quotation formula. That is not the corpus's onset-splice-with-fuller-gloss shape, where the gloss contains the splice's own rendering; it is a false rendering pairing inside the very sentence that warrants holding the unit together across the internal frame. The unit's real seams are unaffected (woe-onset at web:Isa.10.5; close at web:Isa.10.11 before the response formula at web:Isa.10.12): defective warrant element, not alone load-bearing — confirm at medium.

Re-derived: oshb:Isa.10.12 opens וְהָיָ֗ה כִּֽי יְבַצַּ֤ע (byte tier, verse-initial), and a re-sweep of that verse's own consonantal skeleton for the therefore-particle's skeleton finds 0 matches; oshb:Isa.10.16 opens לָ֠כֵן (byte tier, verse-initial) — the genuine particle. The label's only source is the rendering: web:Isa.10.12 opens “Therefore it will happen that when the Lord has performed his whole work on Mount Zion and on Jerusalem,” (web:Isa.10.12) and web:Isa.10.16 likewise opens “Therefore” (web:Isa.10.16), so the English flattens two byte-distinct onsets into one clause type. The shipped 'the two therefore-clauses at web:Isa.10.12 and web:Isa.10.16' is thus a translation-derived clause label — tier-4 rendering data doing clause typology — and it contradicts the row's own rationale, which types the same onset 'A temporal-response formula' (both fields verified verbatim). The rival's rejection stands on grounds independent of the label and no boundary moves: defective warrant inside the rival statement, not alone load-bearing — confirm at medium.

Verified from the shipped fields and re-derived bytes. The rationale's final sentence closes descriptively ('the unit closes with the felled forest' — verified verbatim — with the web:Isa.10.34 quote), naming no ruled closing device and no discriminator; strongest_rejected_alternative treats only the internal web:Isa.10.33 candidate; device_notes' sole rear-edge datum is the mark at oshb:Isa.10.34 (pmarks_Isa.json re-checked: SAMEKH, tier-3, single-witness); and boundary_evidence_refs tops out at web:Isa.10.34 with no web:Isa.11.1 entry (re-read: nothing beyond the span end). The absent discriminator is real and tier-1: וְיָצָ֥א חֹ֖טֶר מִגֵּ֣זַע יִשָׁ֑י (oshb:Isa.11.1, byte tier) opens the next unit verse-initially with a fresh grammatical subject. One correction to the finding's comparative colour: it is not true that every other row in this stretch names its following onset — the refrain stanzas close on the ruled refrain bracket instead, and the row spanning Isa.10.12-Isa.10.19 likewise closes descriptively with no following-onset ref — but that repairs nothing here: this row's close carries neither a ruled closing device nor the following onset, leaving a single-witness tier-3 mark as the only rear-edge support. The boundary itself is sound (the following row argues web:Isa.11.1 and cites web:Isa.10.34): defective rear-seam warrant, not alone load-bearing — confirm at medium.

Re-checked: pmarks_Isa.json carries SAMEKH keyed at MT 10:32 (tier-3, single-witness). Under the mark-closes-its-verse reading the corpus itself applies — this row's device_notes reads its 10:34 mark as closing the unit, and the neighbouring rows read the 9:6-keyed mark (MT 9:6 = WEB 9:7) as following that verse — the break sits at the MT 10:32|10:33 join, the very join the row's disclosed internal candidate opens: הִנֵּ֤ה הָאָדוֹן֙ (oshb:Isa.10.33, byte tier), verse-initial. The two disclosures stand in separate device_notes sentences ('A setumah mark falls inside this unit at oshb:Isa.10.32...' and 'The behold-formula at web:Isa.10.33 is a real internal-seam candidate...' — both verified verbatim) and no wording anywhere in the field names the convergence (checked), so the rival split's strongest corroboration goes undisclosed while both of its halves are disclosed. The mark stays tier-3 and non-driving, holding the unit across it remains legitimate, and per the orchestrator reconciliation note this is a severity item only (span_change false, ruling n/a): a disclosure shortfall — confirm at low.
